Lost in Translation (2003) entire budget for the film was $4 million. It grossed $44.5 million in North America, and $119.7 million world wide.

Sofia Coppola shot large portions of Lost in Translation (2003) illegally on the streets and subways of Tokyo without official filming permits. Because the production could not secure official permissions for most public spaces, the small crew operated under a constant, quiet threat of being stopped or arrested by local authorities.

source_details.title: Lost in Translation
source_details.synopsis: Lost in Translation is a 2003 romantic comedy drama film written and directed by Sofia Coppola. Bill Murray stars as Bob Harris, a fading American movie star who is having a midlife crisis when he travels to Tokyo to promote Suntory whiskey. He befriends another disillusioned American, Charlotte (Scarlett Johansson), a recent college graduate who has been married for two years. The film explores themes of alienation and disconnection against a backdrop of cultural displacement in Japan. It does not use mainstream narrative conventions and is atypical in its depiction of romance. Coppola started writing the film after spending time in Tokyo and becoming fond of the city.
